findings.text: The suite builds every receipt from a SimpleNamespace with hand-named attributes, so it never exercises the real path the deliverable exists for: receipt_from_tree on a ContourTreeArrays, write_receipts/--write, or the --compare CLI exit codes on real receipt files. Add one test that builds a tree via build_contour_tree over a small fixture and round-trips it through write_receipt_file/load_receipts/compare_receipts; a renamed tree attribute would then fail the suite instead of only failing at sweep time. This review verified the real path independently (4 certificate fixtures, 7 fields, identical -> exit 0, one-field mutation -> edge_valid: 1, exit 1) but that is not a committed guard.

justifications.durability: The comparator and its tests are committed with a bodied conventional commit; the gate, negative-control and both suite-arm logs are on disk under the run directory with revisions and literal commands. Durability is marked down because the committed tests exercise only synthetic SimpleNamespace receipts and never call receipt_from_tree/receipt_of/write_receipts/--write or the CLI --compare, so a regression in the real serialization path (a renamed tree attribute) would pass the committed suite even though the comparison logic stays guarded. The review's own end-to-end run closes that gap for this read but is not a committed guard.
justifications.evidence: Every load-bearing claim was reproduced independently in a scratch tree extracted at c01f5f4c3 (module __file__ /tmp/ctta-rc-verify/benchmarks/contour_tree_brute_force.py, cwd /tmp/ctta-rc-verify). The docstring claims that a dropped fixture, or a field missing from one file, counts as a mismatch were also checked directly: a fixture present in only one file counts 1 mismatch in every field, and a field absent from one file counts 1 mismatch in exactly that field.
justifications.fit: The comparator is delivered as a benchmark mode (--write/--compare) matching the followup's 'benchmark mode' phrasing and reuses the existing Fixture/build_contour_tree machinery rather than a parallel implementation. It is a smaller, well-targeted addition. Minor fit note: the negative-control toggle is read from the environment inside the production comparison path rather than injected in the test, so a stray CONTOUR_TREE_RECEIPT_SKIP in the environment would silently omit a field from a real base/head comparison.
justifications.goal_fidelity: Every element of the requested deliverable is present and reproduces: seven-field comparison, one printed line per field with its mismatch count, and a nonzero exit on any mismatch. The reviewed manifest's evidence_inputs overstates the scope of the followup it resolves, claiming item (1) of f-ctta-sweep-durability-and-placement 'is met' when only the comparator half of item (1) is delivered; the performance negative control half of the same item is not committed here. That is a writeback-accuracy issue, not a missing deliverable, so it lowers goal_fidelity by two rather than failing the node.

Work was read-only over the reviewed commit; nothing was written into the repo (the review's writes are the two review-record paths only).
